history.dynasty: Raj Darbhanga patronage (pond; Parvati shrine built 1937)
history.period: Legendary origins in Treta Yuga; Darbhanga-era additions in 20th century
history.summary: TOWN CORRECTION: CSV says Madhubani, but the temple is at Kakraul village in Rahika block, ~9 km from Madhubani town — town field corrected. Legend (per rvatemples): in Treta Yuga sage Kapila came here paying homage to his father sage Kardam, sensed a self-evolved Shiva lingam, worshipped it and named it Kapileshwara Nath; the Mithila Varnana chapter of his Sankhya Shastra is said to record that he awakened the lingam. Compound has two Parvati shrines (the west one with a white marble idol built by Darbhanga Maharaja in 1937), a Vishnu shrine with black-stone idols, Batuk Bhairava to the NW, and a large pond 300 ft NW dug with Raj Darbhanga's help, from which Shravan Jalabhishek water is drawn. Site of Kapila Ashram and the Ancient Mithila University tradition (Wikipedia). Disambiguation: another Kapileshwar Mahadev Mandir exists at Garhbaruari/Baruari, Supaul district — not this temple. Coordinates approximate (POI 'Kakraul' temple at 26.363602, 86.015647; an OSM point labeled 'Kapileshwar, Lord Shiva Temple' sits at 26.35061, 86.00053 — flagged).

name: Kapileshwar Temple
town_description: Rahika is a block headquarters in Madhubani district in the Mithila region of Bihar, set among rice fields and ponds. It is known for the Kapileshwar Shiva temple at Kakraul and as part of the ancient Mithila University tradition.

travel.road: On the Darbhanga–Kaluahi route; ~4 km from Rahika, ~8 km from Madhubani town

visitor_information.best_time: October–March; Maha Shivaratri and Shravan for festival darshan
